production_metadata.production_description:
Correction and resubmission of #2172, which was rejected before proof evaluation because its Lean `4.35.0-rc3` toolchain was unsupported.

Authors: Axel Delaval; Jie Xu; Shitan Xu.

Public library: https://github.com/frenzymath/Jacobian-Challenge

Human direction of the project, strategy, and release; mathematical review of milestone statements. Codex agents developed and adapted Lean proofs, integrated them, and post-processed the formalization into a reusable library. Tools included a formalization graph, task delegation, code search, repository reuse, and Lean/cluster compilation. Parts of the library are adapted from Weil's conjectures project; see NOTICE in the public library.

The submission packages all nine answers for `jacobian_challenge_alggeo` from library commit `dce1ca5941773caba3608dceff56371cefce58ec`, updated to supported stable Lean `4.35.0` with the benchmark-required Mathlib `074063781836922cb02701cd12943c9f51731afa`. The official Challenge, Solution bridge, configuration, and test driver are unchanged. The original library's admitted Challenge is excluded from proof dependencies. The updated package passed its full build (`lake --no-cache build Submission Solution Challenge`) and the unchanged official `lake test` comparator on November 16, 2026: both NanoDa and Lean accepted the solution, and the comparator reported "Your solution is okay!" The checked source digest and stage results are committed in `validation-20261116.json`. Complete auxiliary-model, token, cost, and elapsed-time totals have not been established.

The original formalization was developed through combined Archon Horizon and Codex workflows. See https://arxiv.org/html/2610.08329v1 and the source provenance and third-party notices in the submission repository. This resubmission migrates the public proof to supported Lean 4.35.0 and pinned Mathlib 074063781836922cb02701cd12943c9f51731afa, with unchanged benchmark statements.

This retries smooth Poincaré #2119, whose October 14 evaluation reached the six-hour limit during compilation on the older GitHub-hosted runner. The current standard evaluation runner has 16 CPUs and 32 GB. The exact submitted package passed local compilation and the unchanged official comparator test enforcing both bundled NanoDa and Lean. Source hashes, commands, exit codes, and available console logs are in `reports/evidence/stable-20261116/`. The smooth console capture stopped during the default kernel check after a login interruption; its compute-node completion receipt records official test exit code 0 and stable sources, as documented in the evidence. Local checks used independent Slurm allocations on one node: smooth had 16 CPUs / 60,000 MiB with LEAN_NUM_THREADS=16; topological had 26 CPUs / 100,000 MiB with LEAN_NUM_THREADS=8. Each had its own memory limit and source/build workspace. The final smooth build reused compiled helper artifacts. Because this cluster limits memory mappings to 65,530, a local process restriction selected the stock Lean loader's built-in read/malloc fallback; the submitted build configuration does not include this workaround. These timings do not establish a cold hosted runtime or guarantee completion within six hours. This snapshot contains only the smooth benchmark package.

This is also a retry of #2193, whose evaluation failed in the source-fetch step with a GitHub API HTTP 403 before Lean compilation or kernel checking started. The exact validated source commit is unchanged. The repository is public; the parallel topological evaluation fetched it successfully, and a subsequent unauthenticated API check returned HTTP 200.

The subsequent attempt #2195 successfully fetched the source but failed during Lean environment setup: the GitHub release download for the elan installer returned HTTP 502. This retry again uses the same validated source commit; neither attempt reached submission compilation or proof checking.

Authors: FrenzyMath (PKU@AI4maths): Axel Delaval; Leheng Chen; Zhiyuan Zhang.

Public library: https://github.com/frenzymath/Poincare-Conjecture

Retry of #2194 using the same validated source commit after its standard evaluation reached the six-hour deadline (`evaluation_timeout`), without a final proof verdict. Companion smooth submission #2196 passed. We are retrying the standard tier because the earlier topological run recorded slower compilation on identical shared sources.

The original formalization was developed through combined Archon Horizon and Codex workflows. See https://arxiv.org/html/2610.08329v1 and the source provenance and third-party notices in the submission repository. This resubmission migrates the public proof to supported Lean 4.35.0 and pinned Mathlib 074063781836922cb02701cd12943c9f51731afa, with unchanged benchmark statements.

This retries topological Poincaré #2113, whose October 14 evaluation reached the six-hour limit during compilation on the older GitHub-hosted runner. The current standard evaluation runner has 16 CPUs and 32 GB. The exact submitted package passed local compilation and the unchanged official comparator test enforcing both bundled NanoDa and Lean. Source hashes, commands, exit codes, and available console logs are in `reports/evidence/stable-20261116/`. Local checks used independent Slurm allocations on one node: smooth had 16 CPUs / 60,000 MiB with LEAN_NUM_THREADS=16; topological had 26 CPUs / 100,000 MiB with LEAN_NUM_THREADS=8. Each had its own memory limit and source/build workspace. The final topological build reused helpers compiled in a preceding 5h13m local build under its distinct package name. That build passed, but its test encountered stale local dependency paths; correcting the unsubmitted overrides preserved all package source hashes and compiled helpers. Because this cluster limits memory mappings to 65,530, a local process restriction selected the stock Lean loader's built-in read/malloc fallback; the submitted build configuration does not include this workaround. These timings do not establish a cold hosted runtime or guarantee completion within six hours. This snapshot contains only the topological benchmark package.
